why: PieZ is the pizza restaurant on the 6th Street plaza in Rancho Coronado, Santo Domingo, used by 'There Is A Light That Never Goes Out' for the last-supper table scene. Its building, interior and mirror are ordinary world geometry, but the staff/front-of-house community is only switched on by the sq023 restaurant-scene branch of the district community phase, and the ambient patrons live in a quest-design prefab that only instantiates while the side job runs. This proposal restores normal business: the two vendor bartenders with their local guests, sixteen background customers seated around the room, and the non-scene variant of the restaurant device set.

open_questions: Whole-community form vs vanilla's literal node: vanilla activates #sq023_com_restaurant_background with entry None and phase 'restaurant', while this proposal uses the brief's optional whole-community form None/None. That is equivalent only if whole activation uses entriesInitialState (every entry's initial phase is restaurant). All 16 entries also carry entryActiveOnStart 0, so the tour must confirm they really appear.

var_sq023_restaurant semantics are inferred, not read: the only vanilla action is show 0 when sq023_restaurant_scene_on clears. Whether 0 hides the staged banquet set (normal look, as assumed) or part of the ordinary furnishing is the main thing to verify in game; if 0 strips the room, drop the toggle and leave the prefab default.

How much of the long-table banquet geometry is baked into #sq023_pr_restaurant_clinic rather than governed by the variant: if the table stays visible with the variant at 0, the restaurant will read as a banquet hall and the background patrons' spots may collide with it.
The 17 background-patron spots are only ever exercised inside the quest-staged prefab; confirm they are not floating, inside furniture, or behind the bar.

PieZ's street-front entrance is not a quest-driven door in the extracted device set (only TVs resolve at this location), so there is no door note to give. Confirm the storefront is open/usable in the clean slate; if a cooked door blocks it, it needs a runtime door-policy scope entry.

The proximity anchor is a TVControllerPS because it is the only device the catalogue resolves here; the #tv_1_q003 device actions in the catalogue are All Foods name collisions, so the anchor is a plain restaurant TV and its distance/streaming should be checked on the tour.

communities.why: PieZ's normal front-of-house community: two vendor bartenders (Character.VendorMale) at the bar, a CitizenAldecaldosMale and a CitizenAldecaldosFemale guest, and one decoset entry whose initial phase is 'disabled'. All entries start active with relaxed bar/table/standing workspots, so whole-community Activate puts staff and customers in the room without any quest scene. Vanilla only reaches this node through std_rcr's sq023_restaurant_scene_on > 0 branch (then deactivate, wait, reactivate when the scene is off again); that fact is never set in the clean slate, so the branch stalls and the restaurant is empty.

Seventeen ambient patrons (Character.sq023_customers, _man_a, _man_b, _woman_fat) in the 'restaurant' phase, each on an ordinary chair, table, barstool, vending-machine or arcade workspot - the restaurant's background crowd, not the eight 'last_supper' clients. Their initial phase is already 'restaurant', so whole-community Activate reproduces vanilla's Activate None/restaurant from sq023_ride_to_restaurant. Tour check because this population has only ever been seen while the quest prefab stages the room.

variant_toggles.why: The only vanilla variant at this location is the restaurant-scene set on the device prefab. sq023_restaurant hides it (show 0) exactly when sq023_restaurant_scene_on is cleared, i.e. 0 is the state vanilla itself leaves the world in when the scene is over. Pinning 0 keeps the venue in its non-scene, open-for-business look instead of the staged table set.

proximity_wait.why: The only device the catalogue resolves to a real entity at the restaurant is a TVControllerPS in the location's device prefab. It sits in the room the staff and patrons use, so it streams in exactly when a player walks into PieZ; the cafe's street frontage has no quest-driven door device in the extracted data.
